hyps.why: Replacing a missing direct input-to-output edge with an identity path restores a short gradient-friendly route, gaining far more than replacing an existing convolution.
Adding a 3x3 conv where the direct edge was absent gives a large gain, versus a small gain when replacing skip, pooling or 1x1 ops.
A skip already gives the identity path, so upgrading it to a conv yields less benefit than filling an empty or weak slot.
With the direct edge missing, an identity path from node 1 to the output helps much more than when edge 3 already provides one.
When edge 3 is absent, edge 4 carries more of the output signal, so improving it matters more.
Without the direct edge, an extra identity route into node 2 adds useful connectivity that is redundant otherwise.
Filling a missing first edge with a conv adds a feature path, gaining more than swapping between existing ops.
If edge 3 is absent the output depends on edges 4 and 5, so a stronger edge 5 matters much more.
Adding an identity edge where none existed creates a new path, whereas replacing a conv with skip loses capacity.
With edge 1 removed, edge 0 only feeds node 1 and its upgrade has little route to benefit accuracy.
